keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The infobox of the page gives no area, the body 738 km2 (Zone A 222.5 km2 and Zone B 515.5 km2); Natural Earth's Trieste province (about 210 km2), the three Slovene municipalities and the circle add up to the same order, within a factor of two. Zone A ran from the coast south of Trieste to the Italian border; the Morgan Line (agreed at Duino on 10 June 1945) was the line between the zones, and the Morgan Line page says Pula was an Allied-administered enclave inside Zone B of the 1945 line (its later fate is not on the page).

ledger.note: 15 September 1947: the Free Territory of Trieste comes into existence. It was 'established on 10 February 1947, by a protocol of the Treaty of Peace with Italy' and 'came into existence on 15 September 1947'; 738 km2, about 330,000 people. The Morgan Line page: 'The Morgan Line ceased to exist on 15 September 1947'.

ledger.note: October 1954: Zone B and nine villages go to Yugoslavia. 'Zone B was to be annexed by Yugoslavia, along with nine villages previously in Zone A'; the Morgan Line page says four of them (Plavje, Spodnje Škofije, Elerji, Hrvatini) 'were annexed to Yugoslavia'. The pages do not date the Yugoslav takeover, so the month follows the Zone A handover; the borders were formalised in 1975 at Osimo.

ledger.note: 5 October 1954: the London Memorandum ends the Free Territory. 'On 5 October 1954, the dispute was resolved when the London Memorandum was signed' by the US, UK, Italy and Yugoslavia; no governor was ever appointed (the Soviet Union rejected 12 nominees between October 1947 and March 1948) and the Tripartite Powers had recommended a return to Italian sovereignty on 20 March 1948.

certainty.note: The outer border was fixed by the 1947 peace treaty and the line between the zones followed the Morgan Line of 1945; the pages give no coordinates, so Zone B is approximated by municipalities and a circle.

notes: Requested as a counterpart by eu-22-a. A state Cliopatria lacks (its Yugoslavia row holds two cells of the province of Trieste for 1946-1991, wrong after 26 October 1954, per eu-22-a). Pages differ on one point: the article dates the full-control declaration to 26 October 1954 and the Italian troops' arrival to 25 October. The page is silent on the Belgrade Agreement of 9 June 1945 (it names only Duino, 10 June 1945), on the day of the Yugoslav takeover of Zone B, and on the Treaty of Osimo's day (1975, ratified 1977). The 1 May to 12 June 1945 Yugoslav occupation of Trieste (partisans entered 1 May; withdrew 12 June; Tito accepted 23 May / 9 June) precedes the life of this state and belongs to the Yugoslavia and Italy dossiers; I did not model it. Gazetteer: Zone B uses a lon/lat circle (13.58 E, 45.38 N, 22 km) for the Croatian Buje district; Umag, Buje and Novigrad are not in the gazetteer's places (names wanted).
